title: Complexity means our perception and analysis fail to find a short description

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complexity means our perception and analysis fail to find a short description

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: To call something complex is to say that our methods of perception and analysis have failed to find a short description of the features of it that we are interested in; complexity therefore depends on which features one chooses to capture.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 10: Processes of Perception and Analysis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: when we say that something seems complex, what we are effectively saying is that our powers of perception and analysis have failed on it.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 10, “Processes of Perception and Analysis”; section “Defining Complexity” (from p. 557), p. 557. Scope: the definition of complexity

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch10-06: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.13

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Experiments could study human judgments of complexity, but those judgments would not establish the proposed semantic definition. The claim lacks a distinct empirical outcome that would refute it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The statement stipulates how the word complexity should be interpreted and explicitly makes it relative to chosen features; no dataset can select this definition over other coherent definitions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Alternative complexity measures need not yield the same ordering.

Definitional claim.

Features of interest and shortness are observer-relative.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Wolfram defines apparent complexity as the failure of our perception and analysis to find a short description of the features we care about. That is a conceptual identification, and the dependence on chosen features is part of the definition rather than a parameter to estimate. No public measurement would confirm or refute it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim equates calling something complex with a failure to find a short description of chosen features. Changing which features are chosen changes the verdict by the claim's own terms, so there is no independent measurement that would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Complexity is defined relative to the observer's chosen features, so the claim cannot fail against an observer-independent dataset.

The sentence is an account of what the word means, not a prediction about particular objects.
